purpose: Verified map of the current Titan Zero agent runtime, tool/capability contracts, invocation context, delegation flow, and authority/mutation boundaries. This map documents existing authority; it does not create a parallel runtime.

layers.responsibility: Authority-neutral request/interactions context and correlation identity.
verified: InteractionContext requires company_id and canonical zero/go/hub surface.
correlation_id, request_id, conversation_id and operation_id exist as context fields.
authority_neutral is required true.

layers.responsibility: Deterministic native workforce planning that proposes commands but does not grant execution authority.
verified: Native dispatch/invoicing/rebooking/quote/CRM planning produces proposals/commands.
Server route overwrites company_id from authenticated session where supported.
Proposal structures explicitly keep execution_permitted/grants_authority false where defined.

layers.responsibility: Deterministic discovery of capabilities, tools and atomic worker bindings.
verified: Capability registry scopes module contributions by company_id when a company scope exists.
Tool registry requires canonical company boundary company_id.
Tool definitions must set grants_execution_authority=false.
Atomic worker bindings must not grant authority or delegation rights.
DecisionPacket requires company_id, evidence, risk, source provider/revision and recommended actions.
Decision adapters project/correlate domain evidence into DecisionPacket structures.
DecisionPacket can state authority_required but is not itself execution authority.
Authority evaluation binds company_id, worker, capability, operation/action, risk, approval and autonomy evidence.
Critical risk is denied; protected/high-risk work escalates or requires approval/evidence.
Self-approval is forbidden.
Identity, role, module activation, provider/model/node identity and trust do not positively grant authority.
Distributed placement/trust can constrain eligibility but cannot create business authority.
Business Ops role snapshots are affordance contracts only; server routes remain authoritative.

layers.responsibility: Mutation handoff contract, replay/idempotency binding and authoritative execution evidence.
verified: prepareGovernedCommandEnvelope requires company_id, actor/action/capability/operation/idempotency and an ALLOW authority decision.
High-risk work requires approval refs, evidence refs and known reversibility; critical mutations are denied.
Envelope declares execution_transport=titan-command-bus, direct_mutation=false and authority_effect=false.
Replay binding covers authority proof, context, approvals, evidence, reversibility and expected effect.
Authoritative execution receipts and post-action verification are bound back to command/company/correlation context.

layers.responsibility: Organizational routing and handoff proposals from orchestrator/management layers to atomic workers.
verified: Delegation is proposal-only and requires later authority/capability evaluation.
Atomic workers cannot delegate further.
Delegation, worker identity and tool binding explicitly do not confer authority.

layers.responsibility: Native Business Ops commands, route materialization, role affordances and risk classification.
verified: Command ids/methods/routes/mutating flags and allowed roles are server-owned definitions.
Command risk classification derives from company_id and command evidence.
Shared Business Ops action roles do not substitute for server-side authorization.

layers.responsibility: Authenticated web handoff from workforce agent command selection to native Business Ops routes.
verified: Gateway checks known command, role and entity id and stamps company/user context.
Gateway assesses risk and routes to workforce metadata before execution.
Current executeWorkforceCommand performs a direct same-origin fetch to the native Business Ops API route.
layers.gap: This gateway does not currently prove that mutating commands were wrapped by prepareGovernedCommandEnvelope / canonical Titan Command Bus before the fetch. Downstream route authorization may still be correct, but canonical governed-mutation convergence is not established at this handoff.

current_gaps.summary: Invocation context is distributed across InteractionContext, plan APIs, command metadata and execution-boundary context rather than one canonical agent invocation envelope.

Capability/tool/action discovery authority is spread across capability registry, tool registry, Business Ops command catalogues and decision adapter registry; consolidation must avoid creating a second registry authority.
Web workforce mutating command handoff does not itself demonstrate canonical Command Bus/governed-envelope traversal before same-origin API execution.

exclusions.rule: Titan Code is not part of the Titan Zero production agent runtime and must not become a runtime dependency.

conclusion: The current Titan Zero agent runtime already contains strong reusable authority, capability, delegation and execution primitives. Remaining work is convergence: unify invocation/correlation, establish one deterministic discovery authority, and ensure every mutating workforce path demonstrably traverses the governed command boundary rather than creating parallel runtime logic.
